---
title: "The Viz Gallery: Community-Driven Art"
---

The core philosophy of SPARMVET is that visualizations shouldn't be locked behind complex code. The **Viz Gallery** is the beating heart of this philosophy.

## Purpose of the Gallery

The Gallery serves two massive purposes for the community (be it biologists, economists, or data analysts):
1. **Inspiration:** Not sure what plot best suits your data? Browse the gallery to see what peers have built and discover new analytical angles.
2. **Instant Examples:** Every plot in the Gallery isn't just a picture; it's a full *example*. You can copy the exact YAML logic used to build that plot and paste it into your own data analysis recipe.

## Submitting to the Gallery

If you build a plot in the dashboard that you are proud of, we emphatically encourage you to submit it to the Gallery. If the gallery grows and is useful for people, it will ultimately benefit everybody using it to make it even better.

The Gallery is a **static reference browser** — there is no in-app upload button or admin
review queue. Submitting an example is a file-based, repository convention: you add files
under `assets/gallery_data/` and regenerate the gallery's index.

### Requirements for Submission
Before you submit, your bundle must contain specific metadata to ensure you are credited and the context is preserved:

1. **Authors & Citations:** Provide your name, your team's name, or the publication citation if this plot was used in a manuscript. This allows the community to acknowledge and cite your work. This goes in `example_meta.md`.
2. **A documented transformation chain:** `example_meta.md` should explain *why* the data analysis recipe's wrangling steps do what they do (e.g. "Filtered out calves because they skewed the baseline"). This teaches others how to think about their data. (This is a Gallery authoring convention, separate from HOME's mandatory per-node `reason` field in the Tier 3 audit trail — see [The Audit Pipeline](audit_pipeline.qmd) for that mechanism.)
3. **Data Agnostic Aim:** Try to label your plots in a way that others can understand, even if they aren't studying the exact same pathogen or economic model.

### Submission Process

Every gallery entry is a directory under `assets/gallery_data/` containing the **Scientific
Triplet** (plus its rendered preview) — four files, exactly named:

1. **`data_analysis_recipe.yaml`** — the executable data analysis recipe (`info:` block with
   all six taxonomy fields below, plus the `analysis_groups`/plot spec).
2. **`example_data.tsv`** — a representative, tab-separated dataset.
3. **`example_meta.md`** — the authorship, citation, and transformation-logic write-up
   (3-tier structure: `##` name, a `>` taxonomy tag-strip, then `###` content sections).
4. **`preview_plot.png`** — the rendered evidence of the visualization.

To submit:

1. Create your bundle directory under `assets/gallery_data/` with the four files above.
2. Generate the preview image (overwrites `preview_plot.png`):
   ```bash
   .venv/bin/python libs/viz_gallery/assets/generate_previews.py --only <your_bundle_name>
   ```
3. Regenerate the Gallery's pivot index so the UI picks up your bundle:
   ```bash
   .venv/bin/python libs/viz_gallery/assets/refresh_gallery.py
   ```
4. Open a pull request with your new bundle directory. A bundle missing a required taxonomy
   field is excluded from the index automatically — fix any warnings `refresh_gallery.py` reports
   before submitting.

## Gallery Taxonomy & Sidebar Filters

Every example is classified across **six axes**. These axes power the sidebar filter panels in the Gallery tab — selecting a value narrows the example list in real time.

| Icon | Axis | What it captures |
|------|------|-----------------|
| 📊 | **Family (Purpose)** | The analytical purpose: `Comparison`, `Distribution`, `Correlation`, `Evolution`, `Part-to-Whole`, `Ranking` |
| 🔢 | **Data Pattern** | The shape of the input data (e.g. `1 Numeric, 1 Categorical`) |
| 📈 | **Difficulty** | `Simple` / `Intermediate` / `Advanced` |
| ⚙️ | **Primary Geom** | The main plotnine layer (e.g. `geom_violin`, `geom_bar`, `geom_point`) |
| 🎯 | **What it Shows** | The chart's primary message: `distribution`, `trend`, `ranking`, `relationship`, … |
| 📏 | **Sample Size** | Whether the example needs large n (`large`, `medium+`) or works on any aggregated data (`any`) |

Authors must populate all six fields in the `info` block of their `data_analysis_recipe.yaml` before a submission is accepted. Full allowed-value lists, the data analysis recipe block format, and the `example_meta.md` tag-strip convention are in the [VizFactory Component Gallery appendix](../appendix/viz_factory_components.qmd#gallery-taxonomy-6-axis-classification).
